shoal_e15_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_entry.text: On Day Three Hundred Thirty-One, the room board acquired a line of people before the wage office opened. Yue arrived for her own four-hour receiving shift and found the housing clerk already arguing about the meaning of near. A landlord had described his rooms as near the quay. For a healthy walker with no bags, they were. For someone returning with a child and water jars, the slope between them was part of the rent.

shoal_e15_open_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_open_02.text: The clerk was not offering a public relocation command. Current rooms belonged to actual landlords under their own accepted leases. Families would choose whether to visit, negotiate, remain, or seek a different town. The fire had changed what some households could afford, but it had not granted the wage office authority over where they lived. He Ming wanted that stated aloud before another visitor mistook a useful notice for a summons.

shoal_e15_open_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_open_03.text: A worker named Duan Cai brought his sister Duan Fen to the board. Cai liked the quieter inland rooms. Fen repaired sails near the quay and would lose customers if each small alteration required a long uphill walk. They owned a shared cart and disagreed over who ought to use it on a working day. Their question was not whether the office cared about families. It was whether two livelihoods could fit one proposed move.

shoal_e15_open_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_open_04.text: Another household, led by a woman named Wen Li, wanted to remain within hearing of the first tide bell. Her father had missed a bell while staying with a cousin inland and lost a day's ordinary dock work. He was not injured, merely tired and angry about aging. Li wanted an entrance her youngest child could use safely. The room she could afford close to the quay had a step that made those preferences collide.

shoal_e15_open_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_open_05.text: The landlords had accepted specific viewing windows. The inland window and the quay-block window overlapped on Day Three Hundred Thirty-Five, when Yue had no paid shift. Both households asked whether she would accompany them as an ordinary additional listener, receiving no housing authority or fee. They would inspect and negotiate for themselves. She could be present at one offered visit. Neither was entitled to turn her spare morning into a solution for every household on the board.

shoal_e15_open_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_open_06.text: Before either visit, He Ming organized an ordinary evening discussion in a borrowed room whose owner accepted the limited hours. People brought their own stools where permitted, and three stayed standing because they preferred it. No one was required to reveal a wage figure. He asked them to name costs the advertisements missed. A fisher mentioned water, a grandmother named stairs, and a boy said his friend was on the opposite side of town.

shoal_e15_open_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_open_07.text: The boy's mother initially laughed at the last objection. Then she asked who would watch him after school if they moved away from that friend and the friend's aunt. What sounded like a child's preference included an adult care arrangement. The aunt had her own limits and could not follow every relocating household. Yue wrote nothing until they agreed which ordinary facts belonged on the public question list. Their private quarrels remained private.

shoal_e15_open_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_open_08.text: Rong Sui attended because new charcoal deliveries would need current receiving addresses. He disliked being treated as the answer to every household's cold stove. He could quote an actual price and delivery route. He could not provide indefinite free fuel because a move had been difficult. A worker challenged his minimum delivery size. Rong listened, then offered a smaller shared delivery only if consenting purchasers actually placed and paid the combined order.

shoal_e15_open_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_open_09.text: Nobody bought charcoal merely to keep the meeting harmonious. Two households wanted to consider the offer; another had a different supplier. Rong left with a future quote, not completed sales. He Ming said the meeting could end without an agreement. That permission made the last discussion more useful. People stopped repeating which plan was best for everyone and began asking whether a particular room would let their particular work continue.

shoal_e15_open_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_open_10.text: On Day Three Hundred Thirty-Two, Yue received the third twenty-five-copper weekly settlement for five completed receiving shifts. The third separate two-copper restitution installment also reached her under the actual order. Six of the eight documented clinical copper had now been repaid. The final two remained scheduled for the next date. She kept the ordinary figures because received money paid present costs, while a future installment could not be spent tonight.

shoal_e15_open_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_open_11.text: At her lodging, the innkeeper offered a lower rate if she accepted a much longer stay. Yue declined because her current port work ended on a named date and no next road role had been accepted. The offer was sensible for some guests. It would tie her to a room she might not use. She paid the current ordinary rate and discovered that deciding against a bargain could still feel like losing something.

shoal_e15_open_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_open_12.text: The following evening Song Mei rehearsed with a musician whose fiddle had an old crack that he knew how to accommodate. She wanted a faster passage; he wanted one she could sing after an actual full performance without exhausting her breath. They disagreed in ordinary voices until she tried both. Yue passed the open door and heard the difference. Neither artist needed a cultivation examiner to decide whose knowledge mattered to the work.

shoal_e15_open_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_open_13.text: Jin stopped at the room board on Day Three Hundred Thirty-Four. Bo wanted a ground-floor entrance and hoped to keep his shop, but they had not chosen a lease. She asked the housing clerk about actual costs, then went home to discuss them. The care deposit could not pay a new private rent outside its scope. Their options included staying for now. Nobody would mark that decision as a refusal to recover properly.

shoal_e15_open_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_open_14.text: Yue read the two households' current visit requests again. Duan Cai and Duan Fen wanted a second listener on the inland slope. Wen Li and her father wanted one at the quay-block entrance and lease discussion. An additional person could notice a detail or remember an offered term, but each household retained the answer. Yue would need to give the unchosen household a clear refusal before its accepted viewing hour arrived.

shoal_e15_visit_choice.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_visit_choice.text: On her unassigned morning, Yue could accompany one offered housing visit. Cai and Fen would inspect inland rooms against two competing livelihoods. Li's household would examine a quay-block entrance and the lease keeping them near the tide bell. Yue would be an ordinary listener, not a landlord or household decision-maker. The other household could visit without her and would keep its own choices.

choices.text: Walk the inland route with Cai and Fen.
Visit the quay-block rooms with Li's household.

shoal_e15_inland_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_inland_01.text: Cai carried the shared cart up the first slope without a load. Fen asked him to stop halfway and imagine the sailcloth she would bring home after work. He said the cart had good wheels. She said good wheels did not make the hill disappear. Yue walked beside them and watched where rain had cut a shallow gutter across the road. A room could be affordable while its ordinary approach consumed more work than an advertisement admitted.

shoal_e15_inland_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_inland_02.text: The landlord met them at the accepted time and opened the rooms they had actually requested. He had not promised the ground floor, and its current tenant had not agreed to leave. Fen examined the upper entrance without blaming that tenant for occupying it. Cai liked the light at the western window. Fen opened the cupboard and found enough dampness to ask about the last leak. The landlord answered that the roof repair was scheduled, not yet performed.

shoal_e15_inland_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_inland_03.text: Yue asked whether the present offer included a dry storage space for work materials. It did not. A nearby shed might be separately leased, but its owner was absent and no permission had been secured. Fen said a possible shed could not count as part of today's room. The landlord agreed and corrected the spoken description. Cai looked disappointed. He had already placed his imagined workshop there in the time it took to climb the stairs.

shoal_e15_inland_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_inland_04.text: They went outside to measure the cart's actual turn into the yard. It fit empty. A loaded sail roll would project beyond its handles and need different maneuvering. Cai borrowed no energy from Yue's body or borrowed device to prove an unsuitable load could be moved. He and Fen used an ordinary cord to mark its dimensions. The result gave them a practical question: could they keep their work near the quay while sleeping inland?

shoal_e15_inland_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_inland_05.text: Fen wanted to calculate the separate rents before answering. Cai wanted one night to think in a quieter place. She reminded him that a pleasant viewing hour was not the sound of that road during heavy rain. The landlord allowed a second ordinary visit within a new accepted window, without charging them for a lease they had not taken. Yue noted the offered time when they asked her to remember it.

shoal_e15_inland_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_inland_06.text: On the walk back, the siblings stopped at a stall selling boiled beans. Cai paid for his own bowl and offered Fen one from his actual purse. She accepted, then said accepting lunch did not mean accepting the move. He laughed because he had been preparing exactly that argument. Yue paid for her portion and stayed outside their bargain. The visit had given her three people with ordinary appetites rather than a housing problem waiting for a heroic answer.

shoal_e15_inland_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_inland_07.text: At the quay-block visit, Wen Li's household inspected without Yue. Her father listened to the tide bell from the doorway and preferred the familiar distance. Li asked about the step and found a removable ramp was not included in the current lease. She decided to keep looking before committing. A missing additional listener did not erase her judgment. Yue would later hear only the result she chose to offer, not pretend she had witnessed every conversation.

shoal_e15_inland_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_inland_08.text: Cai and Fen returned to their present room with the landlord's actual written offer. They declined the current upper rooms after calculating the combined sleeping and work costs. Cai regretted the window. Fen regretted disappointing him. Neither regret changed their answer. They asked the clerk to notify them if a separately suitable ground-floor room became available, without claiming a reservation the landlord had never made.

shoal_e15_inland_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_inland_09.text: Yue's presence had helped catch the absent storage promise before it became a shared assumption. Fen thanked her for that particular question. Cai thanked her for not treating his wish for quiet as childish. The siblings still had crowded rooms and different preferred futures. Their decision had prevented an unsuitable lease, not supplied the perfect one. The public room could record the declined offer and continue its actual work.

shoal_e15_inland_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_inland_10.text: That evening Fen showed Yue a small sail patch made from scraps too short for her clients' larger jobs. She had stitched a fish along its edge as a joke for Cai. It belonged to her, and she was not offering it to the port's public display. Yue admired it where it lay on the table. A visit could create a modest private acquaintance without creating permission to publish someone's art or to speak for their household.

shoal_e15_inland_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_inland_11.text: Cai later walked the inland road alone at the second accepted viewing time. He wanted to know how noisy it grew after sunset, even though they had declined the present rooms. The landlord understood the narrower purpose and allowed it. Cai returned with a different opinion about the route's water jars and dogs. He had learned something useful beyond winning the argument, which Fen considered a promising change.

shoal_e15_inland_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_inland_12.text: Before her next shift, Yue told the housing clerk only the facts the siblings had permitted for their current receiving record: the actual offer, the absent included storage, and their decline. She did not give the office their lunch argument or Fen's stitched fish. Their public housing question now had clearer edges. Wen Li's separate household question remained its own. The town had room for two refusals that meant different things.

shoal_e15_quay_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_quay_01.text: Wen Li met Yue beside the tide bell's ordinary approach. Her father arrived carrying the child because he liked doing it and was currently able, not because the prospective room had already solved its entrance. Li asked him to set the child down before they examined the step. The landlord had agreed to this viewing hour. A porter passing with a real load asked them to leave room on the public lane.

shoal_e15_quay_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_quay_02.text: The threshold was higher than the advertisement's photograph suggested. Li measured it with an ordinary rule she had brought herself. The landlord said a removable ramp might be fitted later, at separate cost and with the lane authority's permission. Yue repeated the two conditions when Li asked whether she had heard them correctly. Nobody counted a possible later ramp as an installed feature of today's offer.

shoal_e15_quay_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_quay_03.text: Li's father stood in the room while the tide bell rang. He could hear it through the ordinary open window. That mattered to his working day, and Li did not dismiss it simply because the entrance concerned her more. The landlord proposed a longer lease at a lower daily equivalent. Yue asked where the early departure charge appeared. He pointed to a line that Li had not yet reached in the actual terms.

shoal_e15_quay_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_quay_04.text: Li sat on a stool the landlord offered and read the line carefully. Her work might move again if a current customer changed warehouses. A lower price tied to a longer obligation could cost her more than the shorter term. She asked for the ordinary short lease price and its actual dates. The landlord gave them without promising that another tenant would wait while she considered a future she had not yet chosen.

shoal_e15_quay_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_quay_05.text: The child discovered a crack in the courtyard wall and announced that a beetle lived there. Her grandfather knelt to look, using his own ordinary body and time. Li continued asking about water access. The landlord answered the question that had been asked instead of selling the beetle's courtyard as proof that families should accept. Yue liked the child's interest and the adult's attention; neither was evidence about whether a lease would work.

shoal_e15_quay_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_quay_06.text: On the lane, Li asked her father whether he would accept a room farther from the bell if the entrance was easier. He said he might, provided he had a current ordinary way to wake on time. She offered to discuss a shared clock purchase from their own money. He objected to the price, then admitted missing another day's wage might cost more. Their agreement would require actual numbers, not a promise that love would make the clock free.

shoal_e15_quay_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_quay_07.text: Meanwhile, Cai and Fen visited the inland rooms without Yue. Fen asked about work storage and learned the separate shed was not included or presently available by permission. They declined the upper rooms after comparing their combined costs. Cai still liked the western light. A household could reach a practical answer without the extra listener it had requested. Yue did not claim their discernment as a benefit of her absent presence.

shoal_e15_quay_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_quay_08.text: Li declined the longer quay-block lease and requested its shorter actual offer to take home. She had not accepted a ramp that did not exist. The landlord gave the permitted written terms and named the day when a new reply was needed. Her father helped the child step out, watching the threshold with the care he would have to use every morning. The room remained available for a household whose preferences fit it better.

shoal_e15_quay_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_quay_09.text: Yue's added question had brought the early departure charge into the discussion before Li considered signing. Li thanked her for remembering to ask. Yue had not chosen the household's future or made the landlord dishonest. The charge had been in the offered terms. An ordinary second listener could be useful because attention was finite, particularly when a parent was reading a lease while also watching a child at an unfamiliar doorway.

shoal_e15_quay_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_quay_10.text: Later Li invited Yue to a cup of tea in her current room. The invitation was private and finite. Her father showed the child how his old tide notebook worked, including days crossed out when no wage had been earned. Li asked whether he wanted the child to inherit the book. He said she could inherit it without inheriting his job. The child said she currently intended to be a beetle keeper.

shoal_e15_quay_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_quay_11.text: Li laughed, then became quiet about the next month's rent. She did not ask Yue for a secret fund or a room guaranteed by cultivation. She wanted another listener while she compared the actual short offer with remaining where she was. Yue could offer that ordinary hour and still leave when it ended. The tea did not create a permanent duty to the household or permission to repeat the conversation at the office.

shoal_e15_quay_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_quay_12.text: Before the next shift, Yue returned Li's permitted current housing reply to the clerk: no long lease accepted, short terms requested, entrance alteration still unapproved and unfunded. The office could work with those concrete facts. It did not receive the child's imagined profession or the father's wish for the notebook. Cai and Fen's separate decline also reached the desk through their own message. Two households had kept authority over different answers.

shoal_e15_rejoin_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_01.text: On Day Three Hundred Thirty-Six, the housing board showed fewer available rooms than at the start of the week. Other households had actually accepted some offers. The clerk removed those entries after their proper receiving, leaving no phantom room to make the list look generous. People waiting for a particular entrance could remain waiting. A successful lease elsewhere in town did not mean that everyone at the board had been housed.

shoal_e15_rejoin_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_02.text: Bo attended his third four-copper rehabilitation session under the existing forty-copper support line. The practitioner observed the current leg and allowed a little more of one ordinary movement, while keeping heavy work prohibited. Bo had slept badly and wanted the whole appointment finished quickly. Jin asked whether he wanted her to stay for the explanation. He said yes, with an embarrassment that did not make the request less valid.

shoal_e15_rejoin_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_03.text: Afterward the former apprentice came for the one ordinary evening he had offered. Bo paid the agreed small amount from his own shop money for an actual sorting task within the apprentice's present skills. Bo remained seated under his own limits, identifying fastenings rather than hauling them. They found a drawer mislabeled years before the fire. The apprentice said that explained a season of being scolded for choosing the wrong ones.

shoal_e15_rejoin_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_04.text: Bo apologized without converting the old mistake into a joke that required the apprentice to laugh. The apprentice accepted the apology and wanted to keep the mislabeled drawer as evidence for one more evening. Jin let them argue because the disagreement was about something small enough to finish. Later Bo said he had missed being wrong in a way that could be fixed by changing a label.

shoal_e15_rejoin_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_05.text: On Day Three Hundred Thirty-Seven, the third five-copper restricted-income payment arrived for Bo under the care deposit's finite schedule. Fifteen had now been received, fifteen remained future. The support had not restored his trade's lost season. It helped pay ordinary household costs while he and Jin considered what could actually change. Neither the provider nor Yue required him to announce that the help made him happy.

shoal_e15_rejoin_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_06.text: Wen Li inspected a different current room with her father at its landlord's own accepted time. It was farther from the bell and had a lower entrance. They compared the actual short lease with its water access and road. Her father decided an ordinary clock they could afford together might be worth the distance. They accepted that particular room under a paid short term, keeping future renewal a new decision.

shoal_e15_rejoin_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_07.text: The clock purchase came from their own household money. It was an ordinary used clock inspected by the seller under the sale's terms, not a cultivator's everlasting device. Li's father wound it himself and set it against the public tower before bedtime. The first morning he woke before it rang. He was irritated because he had paid for the help, then laughed when Li asked whether he wanted it to make him oversleep.

shoal_e15_rejoin_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_08.text: Cai and Fen remained in their current room for another paid period they could actually afford. They agreed to keep looking separately at the features each needed and to compare offers together before accepting. Cai made more daytime use of a quiet public corner whose owner permitted short reading visits. It was not a substitute private bedroom. It gave him one piece of the quiet he wanted without claiming the entire housing problem solved.

shoal_e15_rejoin_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_09.text: A family with two elderly adults chose to leave the harbor for relatives inland. The relatives confirmed their offered rooms and actual arrival dates before the family booked road seats from its own means and accepted assistance. The choice was theirs. They did not owe the port a promise to return because their neighbors would miss them. Their old room would become available only after the actual lease ended and the owner received the keys.

shoal_e15_rejoin_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_10.text: At their farewell meal, one neighbor argued that leaving was giving up. The older woman asked what exactly she was required to win. She wanted to sleep near her sister and stop climbing the quay stairs. Her husband wanted to keep a fishing basket because he might visit the river. Their plans did not erase affection for the harbor. The neighbor apologized for turning his own sadness into a command that they remain.

shoal_e15_rejoin_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_11.text: He Ming went to the farewell after his actual work, bringing a paid ordinary loaf rather than charging food to a housing account. Yue shared another contribution. They listened while the departing household described the road it had booked. The youngest cousin wanted to go with them, then changed her mind when her mother explained the actual length of the stay. Every person's longing did not need the same destination.

shoal_e15_rejoin_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_12.text: The packing partnership posted new ordinary labor prices for small repairs. Some suppliers wanted the old prices because money remained tight. Workers wanted the actual extra sorting time recognized. The posted schedule did not force every supplier to order. It gave both sides a current basis for deciding. Rong Sui declined one optional repair at the higher price and accepted another because the damaged container could not safely do its next planned trip.

shoal_e15_rejoin_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_13.text: During her receiving shift, Yue helped distinguish a completed paid repair from a supplier's intention to commission one later. The difference mattered to the worker waiting for money and to the owner who had not authorized the second task. Nobody gained by treating an uncertain future sale as current income. The conversation grew sharp, then precise enough that the actual accepted work could be paid without inventing the rest.

shoal_e15_rejoin_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_14.text: On Day Three Hundred Thirty-Nine, Yue's fourth completed week paid twenty-five copper. The fourth and final two-copper restitution installment also arrived, completing eight copper against the actual documented clinical fees she had paid. The contact order remained separate from the tool owner's property process. Repayment did not require her forgiveness, and completion did not mean he had recovered every lost tool. She could close that ordinary money item without closing all feeling about the shove.

shoal_e15_rejoin_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_15.text: She bought a small bag of fresh greens on her walk home because she wanted a supper with something that had not been salted. The seller asked if she was the woman in the school drawing. Yue asked which drawing. He considered this a fair question and described the revised alarm sheet on the public wall. She confirmed the ordinary receiving role he had actually seen, leaving the imagined flames to the imagined picture.

shoal_e15_rejoin_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_16.text: The greens wilted a little before she reached her room. She had stopped to hear a fiddler test a new passage outside the rehearsal door. Song had refused the first ending because it softened an argument she wanted the listeners to hear. The fiddler tried another. Yue stayed until she could hear why Song preferred it. Then she left them working, bought no secret right to the piece, and cooked the greens while they were still useful.

shoal_e15_rejoin_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_17.text: Bo's second funded ordinary care journey occurred on Day Three Hundred Forty. Four copper paid the accepted carrier, completing the deposit's eight-copper travel line with the first actual journey. The carrier and clinical staff used their own proper roles. Jin brought questions about daily movement and the current brace. Yue heard the completed public account entry later, not a private examination she had not attended.

shoal_e15_rejoin_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_18.text: The review did not clear Bo for heavy hauling. It supported the current limited work and next ordinary assessments. He wanted to visit the shop for longer than his existing plan permitted. The practitioner helped identify an actual safe interval and what should stop it. Bo disliked the shortness of the interval. He accepted it because a longer wish was not the same thing as a stronger leg.

shoal_e15_rejoin_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_19.text: Jin decided not to rent another room yet. Their present entrance remained inconvenient, but two rents would consume money needed for the shop's narrower reopening. Bo agreed after seeing the figures, then asked whether agreement meant he should stop complaining about the stairs. She said she preferred a useful complaint to a silent one. They could keep the difficulty visible while deciding that another current cost was worse.

shoal_e15_rejoin_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_20.text: Yue met them outside after the journey because they had offered an ordinary short conversation. Bo described the former apprentice's triumph over the drawer label. Jin described a client who had tried to pay for one repair with the promise of three future ones. Both wanted to talk about work that was actually theirs. Yue listened without turning the visit into a report on how brave their recovery appeared.

shoal_e15_rejoin_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_21.text: At the quay, a stray dog slept beneath the shade of a cart that was not currently moving. Its owner was a child from the next lane, who arrived breathless to fetch it before the cart's accepted loading time. The dog resisted, then followed a piece of bread. Yue watched the ordinary argument and remembered Bo's chalk-stealing hen. The harbor was large enough to have comedies that did not compensate for anyone's fracture.

shoal_e15_rejoin_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_22.text: A visiting seller offered a charm said to keep storms from a household door. He showed no independently tested method or actual claim a buyer could verify. He Ming asked him to remove the unsupported promise from the partnership room. The seller could sell decorative paper under honest terms elsewhere with permission. He could not borrow the fire's fear to make an unqualified protection sound like a completed safety service.

shoal_e15_rejoin_23.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_23.text: One customer argued that people ought to be allowed hope. He Ming answered that they could hope while knowing what they bought. The disagreement ended without exposing the seller as a secret demon or requiring Yue to fight him. He removed the protection claim from that room's display and lost some buyers. Others bought the decorative paper for its painted crane. Different decisions became possible once the actual object was described.

shoal_e15_rejoin_24.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_24.text: On Day Three Hundred Forty-One, Li's household moved to the accepted lower entrance at the actual carrier hour it had booked and paid. Her father kept the tide notebook in a dry bag. The child inspected the new courtyard for beetles and found none immediately. That disappointment did not invalidate the move. The adults had chosen the place for current costs and access, and they would learn its ordinary inconveniences by living there.

shoal_e15_rejoin_25.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_25.text: Li returned the old room keys under the landlord's actual departure terms. A small repair charge remained disputed because the mark had appeared before their tenancy. The receiving office accepted the available dated evidence and named the next process. The move was not delayed by Yue supplying a final moral judgment. Li paid the undisputed amount and kept the contested portion for its proper resolution.

shoal_e15_rejoin_26.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_26.text: Yue helped at the public room during her assigned hours, where a new tenant asked about the now-vacant old room. Its original step remained. Removing one family's name from the lease had not altered the structure. The clerk stated the entrance accurately before arranging a permitted viewing. A room unsuitable for Li's household could still suit someone else, provided that person received the actual information and chose for themselves.

shoal_e15_rejoin_27.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_27.text: On the third evening after the move, Li's father missed the familiar harbor smell and walked down for a short ordinary visit. He heard the bell, bought a small fish, and returned before darkness made the slope harder. He was not pretending that a clock replaced every part of his old life. His daughter did not require him to praise the new room every day. They had chosen a tradeoff they could discuss without undoing it.

shoal_e15_rejoin_28.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_28.text: Cai found a public notice for an actual quiet daytime job that might fit his present skills. Fen encouraged him to ask about it and declined to promise the household could afford any wage loss during training. He met the employer at its accepted time, learned the lower pay, and chose not to take the current offer. The possible change had been worth examining. Refusal left him with work he knew and a wish still unfulfilled.

shoal_e15_rejoin_29.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_29.text: Fen bought a small ordinary lamp for their room from her received earnings and placed it where Cai could read without disturbing her sleep. The fuel cost stayed with their household. It was a modest adjustment, not a new relay appliance powered by Yue. Cai thanked her and asked what would help her sewing table. They measured the chair she had been complaining about instead of deciding gratitude meant she should stop asking.

shoal_e15_rejoin_30.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_30.text: On Day Three Hundred Forty-Three, Bo completed his fourth four-copper rehabilitation session. Sixteen copper of the session line had now been actually used, with later visits still future. He could manage a little more ordinary movement under the current plan. The practitioner recorded the remaining pain and distance limits rather than allowing a cheerful afternoon to stand for every condition. The brace remained a support, not a certificate for his former heavy work.

shoal_e15_rejoin_31.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_31.text: The practitioner also asked Jin whether the ordinary support task she had learned still fit her own body and schedule. She said one part made her wrist tired. They reviewed a safer actual arrangement and which tasks required qualified help. Bo listened instead of answering for her. Care could burden a partner even when she wanted to offer it. Naming that burden gave them something practical to change.

shoal_e15_rejoin_32.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_32.text: After the session, Bo spent the permitted short interval at his shop. He sat where he could see the drawers and instructed the apprentice who had accepted that day's paid scope. One customer began telling him how fortunate he was. Bo asked which fastening the man needed. The change of subject was blunt and useful. They completed the ordinary sale without requiring him to perform gratitude for a stranger's comfort.

shoal_e15_rejoin_33.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_33.text: Yue was at her own receiving table when a young worker asked whether Bo's shop would take another apprentice. She directed the worker to Bo's actual current notice and warned against assuming a post had been offered. The worker could ask. Bo could decline, accept a limited trial, or wait. The existence of a recovering business did not make every hopeful newcomer its responsibility.

shoal_e15_rejoin_34.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_34.text: On Day Three Hundred Forty-Four, the fourth five-copper restricted-income payment arrived. Twenty of thirty had been received under the finite care schedule. Bo and Jin planned with the money actually present. Two further installments remained accepted future support. Their rent and shop choices remained theirs; the care provider had not purchased a vote in the household by issuing a payment.

shoal_e15_rejoin_35.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_35.text: The older departing household sent a message from the inland road's first actual stop. Their carrier had reached it on the booked day. They disliked one inn's soup and liked seeing hills after years of watching masts. The message did not prove their entire new life would be better. It proved they had traveled that far and wanted the harbor to know they were thinking of the people left behind.

shoal_e15_rejoin_36.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_36.text: He Ming read the permitted greeting at the next ordinary gathering. Someone asked whether their rooms inland were still waiting. He said the current confirmation had come from the relatives before departure and any later update would need an actual message. People laughed at his cautious answer, then asked about the soup. The household's absence was real enough to make the room quieter. Its future did not have to be declared settled to let them wish it well.

shoal_e15_rejoin_37.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_37.text: That night Yue looked at the road notices outside the carrier office. One convoy had left, another was still open, and the route toward the mine had current quoted travel time. She had no accepted outgoing role. Her port appointment still required performed work through its final week. She could be interested in a road without pretending the interest paid a seat or released her from current hours.

shoal_e15_rejoin_38.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_rejoin_38.text: A harbor worker stood beside her reading the same board for a different reason. His sister was expected on a later boat. He wanted to know whether the road connection would bring her before a family meal. The clerk could give current booking information and actual arrivals, not a guarantee against future weather. Yue shared the space silently. The board held many people's roads, of which her eventual choice would be only one.

shoal_e15_close_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_close_01.text: Behind the carrier office, ordinary dock musicians were practicing for a small paid gathering at the end of the week. Their drummer stopped when a loading crew needed to hear a foreman's instructions, then resumed after the cart cleared. Yue recognized the rhythm from an earlier performance but not the new words. A singer had changed them after someone objected to a rhyme. The town's art was work too, with people answering for choices that could be heard.

shoal_e15_close_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_close_02.text: A boy asked whether Yue would stay for the gathering. She said she had not yet decided, and he accepted that answer after asking whether adults ever knew their own evenings. Some did, she told him. He said his mother knew every evening until his uncle arrived and changed supper. Then he ran after the drummer, who had promised to show him one ordinary beat when the rehearsal's actual work was finished.

shoal_e15_close_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_close_03.text: Yue returned to her lodging before the public lane grew dark. She washed the new cup herself and put it beside the old uneven one. Both had cost actual money. The old cup still needed a careful place to stand; the new one made no demand. She used the old one for flowers bought in a small bunch from a grower who had surplus stems. They leaned in a direction the cup seemed determined to encourage.

shoal_e15_close_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e15_close_04.text: Before sleep, she checked the remaining days of her receiving appointment. The last week's work was approaching, with current owners still waiting for qualified findings. Road plans would have to fit after the actual term. She had paid the month's lodging from received wages and savings, with later payments still future. Outside, a carrier's wheels rolled toward a departure already booked by other people. Yue listened until they faded and closed her notebook, leaving the next page for a journey she had yet to accept.
